criteria.criterion: The `mcp` service starts with a usable ticket store, or is explicitly configured and documented as not serving tracker reads.
`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` (or a sibling) asserts the store provisioning, so this gap cannot ship silently again.
`docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` records the decision taken for the three questions above.

Bug 'mcp compose service never provisions a ticket store, so every MCP tracker read on the deployed server is empty' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior now holds in the code.

findings.criterion: `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md` records the decision taken for the three questions above.
findings.detail: The ADR at docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md covers three decisions (exposure/auth, autodeploy, certified-op routing) but does NOT record the ticket store provisioning decisions that were the subject of the three open questions in the bug: (1) whether to serve the shared tickets branch or only certified ops, (2) dedicated volume vs sharing reviewbot-tickets, and (3) read-only or writer. The ADR contains zero occurrences of 'tracker', 'ticket store', 'mcp-tickets', 'read-write', or 'dedicated volume'. The operator design decisions recorded in the ticket comments (full read-write, dedicated volume /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets, fallback to reviewbot PAT) are not reflected in the ADR.
findings.remediation: Update docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md to add a section recording the ticket store provisioning decisions: (1) the server serves the full shared tickets branch (full read-write, not read-only or certified-ops-only), (2) a dedicated volume /var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets is used rather than sharing reviewbot-tickets, and (3) the PAT fallback to reviewbot-tickets-pat when the dedicated slot is blank.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
